s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, slowly growing, exophytic oral lesion
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion present since birth with no change in size or character
Mild contrast enhancement on MRI with intact overlying mucosa
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
Lesion located on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion is 1.5-cm in diameter
Lesion is exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character
Vital signs are within normal limits
MRI shows a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appears partly fatty, likely submucosal
Lesion demonstrates mild contrast enhancement
Intact overlying mucosa
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appear normal

shortlist.label: Lingual lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion appears partly fatty and is located on the midline of the dorsal tongue, consistent with a lipoma

shortlist.label: Congenital granular cell epulis
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion is exophytic, smooth, and has been present since birth, consistent with a congenital granular cell epulis

shortlist.label: Lingual myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion is soft and has a smooth appearance, consistent with a myxoma

shortlist.label: Lingual fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion is exophytic and has a regular shape, consistent with a fibroma

shortlist.label: Congenital lingual hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: The lesion has been present since birth and has a smooth appearance, consistent with a congenital hamartoma

raw.rationale: The lesion's presence since birth, location on the midline of the dorsal tongue, and partly fatty composition are consistent with a congenital lingual hamartoma, which is a rare benign tumor that can contain various tissue types, including fat.

rejected.label: Lingual lipoma
rejected.why: While the lesion appears partly fatty, its location and presence since birth are more suggestive of a hamartoma than a lipoma, which is typically a discrete fatty tumor.

rejected.label: Congenital granular cell epulis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents as a gingival mass, not on the dorsal tongue.

rejected.label: Lingual myxoma
rejected.why: Myxomas are rare and usually do not have a significant fatty component.

rejected.label: Lingual fibroma
rejected.why: Fibromas are typically solid and not partly fatty.
